    🏔 Meteorologist Forecast
    Temira, The Gorge Is My Gym · posted Sat Nov 28 · full post ↗

    Our general picture has quite a bit of rain Sunday and Monday followed by snow Monday night into Tuesday. Through next weekend, temps will be cooler, but under 6” total snowfall is forecast. Things start looking up around the 8thof December, when about 90% of the Euro ensembles bring colder temps and significant snowfall for Mt. Hood. I’m not sure the resorts will open by the weekend of the 12th, but this forecast looks promising for an opening sometime between the 12thand the 14th. The intraquartile range through 12/11 is 18-43” snowfall at 5000′. Fingers crossed!

    Saturday won’t bring any snow to Mt. Hood, but it’ll bring a lot of sunbeams! The free air freezing level rises to 9000-10,000′ this afternoon under mostly sunny sky. Wind will be variable to 15mph through Sunday morning. High clouds arrive overnight.

    Clouds Sunday morning quickly give way to … rain. The snow level hovers between 8000′ and 9000′ during the daylight hours and drops to 7000′ overnight. About 0.4” rain falls during the day followed by 0.8” rain overnight. Wind will be variable to 10mph in the morning and SW/S 20-35 from the afternoon into the night.

    Rain continues Monday daytime, but snow replaces the rain in the evening. The snow level will be 7000′ during the day, 4500′ in the evening, and 3000′ after midnight. During the day, 2.5” rain is forecast. That’s followed by 0.5” mixed precip in the evening and 0.8” water equivalent snowfall overnight with strong WSW wind. This gives us a forecast of 6-10” at 5000′ with a LOT more above 7000′. Wind will be S 20-35 early, WSW 50-60 in the afternoon, and WSW 50 overnight.

    Light snowfall continues Tuesday morning before the sky clears in the afternoon. The snow level will be 3000′ early, 2500′ in the afternoon, and the free air freezing level will be around 1500′ overnight. Just 0.2” WE is forecast in the morning for a couple inches of new snow. Wind: W 30 in the morning, NW 20-30 in the afternoon, and NW 15 overnight.

    Looking at the rest of next week, the forecast contains cooler temps but limited moisture for 1-5” total through the weekend of the 6th. Looking deeper into the future, there are good signs of season-starting snowfall beyond Tuesday the 8th. My fingers are crossed, and my skis are waxed. I’ll be putting on my snow tires on the 9th. Hope to see you on the snow soon!
